objective: Implement asynchronous Action submission, a durable permission-filtered GM inbox and delayed resolution by extending the existing A6 proposal/decision/Event architecture so one durable proposal can survive disconnect/time/device boundaries and still produce at most one final authoritative outcome, without creating a second asynchronous rules engine, queue authority or notification authority.

APW-02.rule: Async play extends ordinary A6 proposal/decision/Event authority; one proposal may produce at most one final authoritative outcome.

APW-07.rule: Stable operation IDs, expected versions, status lookup and Event cursors govern disconnect/ambiguous/retry recovery.

application_baseline.rule: Live A6 inspection proved migration 0004 already owns action_proposals, action_review_claims, action_decisions, action_results, action_history, action_notifications and a6_operations, including proposal-operation uniqueness and one-final-decision-per-proposal. APW-I03 therefore remained migration-free and did not claim 0011.

delivered: Migration-free APW-I03 orchestration port over the existing A6 proposal/decision/Event model.

Deterministic local-alpha/CI transactional service that reuses A6 validation, decision queue projection, notification projection and atomic accepted-result commit boundaries; it is explicitly not production client authority.
Durable pending proposal submission with stable operation identity; same operation/same payload replays prior status and conflicting reuse is rejected.
Permission/visibility filtering occurs before GM inbox count and topology projection.
Review claims are advisory coordination only; current GM authority is rechecked at delayed resolution.
Delayed Session-version drift fails stale intent closed instead of silently recalculating or applying it.
Approved delayed resolution produces one atomic ActionResultCommitted Event and advances Session version once; denial produces no gameplay result Event and no Session-version advance.
Decision retry identity is bound to decision intent rather than retry observation time, so a lost response can be recovered later without becoming a different command.
Player submit/status recovery and GM durable-inbox surfaces exercise Player submit -> later GM review -> Player recovery without a second Action engine.
Nine focused APW-I03 acceptance tests plus the full client regression suite passed on the final exact head.
